task.title: Creating a Survey with a Single Block
task.shortdesc: Creating a Survey with a Single Block.

taskbody.context:
Additional Steps for Creating a Survey With a Single Block
"Blocks" in a survey are used to gate access. For instance, if specific users are meant to see some questions not others, gated by their answer to an early question. That is, if participants in the morning section are meant to see a set of five questions that all refer to their satisfaction with the "April 6th morning session," while afternoon participants are meant to see the same questions with a wording change to state "April 6th afternoon session," blocking can be very useful. Mechanically, participants are guided to a separate subset of questions - a block - depending upon which answer they give to a "gating" multiple-choice question such as "Which session did you participate on?" followed by a series of discreet answer choices.
In this section, the default single question block setup will be used. An initial default question is already provided as a starting point.

step.cmd: To modify the default question, simply click within the box to change text to the desired text.

image.alt: A drop-down menu with several options for how to modify a single question in Qualtrics

step.cmd: Modify question type using the dropdown box at the left side of the screen.

fig.title: Modifying a Single Question Dropdown Menu Closeup

image.alt: A drop-down menu that shows more detailed options for the selected question type.

step.cmd: Each of the possible question types that Qualtrics supports is available from that dropdown menu.
Once the correct question type is selected, type-specific characteristics can be altered from the unique question menus for each type.
Click the slider(s) to add any response validations or requirements, as appropriate.

fig.title: Setting Response Validation and Required Responses

image.alt: A slider bar is used to toggle on the response validation settings.

step.cmd: Add additional questions to the same block by clicking on "Add New Question" and selecting the question type.

fig.title: Adding an Additional Question to the Survey

image.alt: Shows the Button to Click to Add a New Question in Qualtrics

step.cmd: Move questions and reorder by clicking the ... menu item at the top left of the question.
Select "Move Question" from the resulting dropdown menu.

image.alt: Shows the location options to move a question above or below other questions in Qualtrics.

step.cmd: Then select where to move the question from the resulting pop up.

fig.title: Additional Detail to Move a Survey Question

image.alt: Shows More Detail of the Options to Move a Survey Question Relative to Other Questions Within Qualtrics.

info.p: These basic steps will enable any user to create a straightforward feedback survey, planning survey, or otherwise engage with users. More advanced users can refer to additional guides for more detailed guides to block structure, logical skips, and other advanced survey programming.
